bullets: How living things are linked: who eats whom, where the energy goes, and how carbon loops round
slides.heading: Ecology: food webs, energy flow, the carbon cycle
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we trace one food chain link by link, follow the energy as it shrinks up the pyramid, and watch carbon loop - then we separate the one flow that never loops.

bullets: Build a food chain and name producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer and decomposer
Explain why only about a tenth of the energy passes to the next level, and correct the claim that energy is recycled like nutrients
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: keep flows and loops apart in your minds, because our exit ticket will ask you to separate the one-way energy flow from the nutrient loop.

bullets: Nutrients go round and round the ecosystem, used again and again
Energy arrives with sunlight - so does it also circle back to the grass, or does it leave for good?
slides.heading: Does energy loop forever?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if energy looped back like nutrients, would the grass need sunlight at all? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because scene 5 puts the two flows side by side.

bullets: Energy flows one way: sunlight in, heat out, with only about a tenth passed up each level
Nutrients and carbon loop: decomposers return them to soil and air for reuse
A food chain shows the links; an energy pyramid shows the shrinking share
slides.heading: One flow, one loop
slides.notes: Stress the two patterns: flow versus loop. Energy is spent as it travels; matter is recycled and travels round again.

bullets: Grass the producer is eaten by the rabbit, the primary consumer
The fox, the secondary consumer, eats the rabbit - and decomposers finish every link
slides.heading: Food chain: built beat by beat
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and name each role as it appears: producer, primary consumer, secondary consumer, decomposer.

bullets: Only about a tenth of the energy at one level reaches the next
That is why top carnivores are few: the energy runs out up the pyramid
slides.heading: Energy pyramid: only about 10% passes up
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and pause at each step up: ask where the other nine tenths went - mostly lost as heat.

bullets: Plants absorb carbon dioxide in photosynthesis - a sink
Animals and decomposers return it by respiration - a source
slides.heading: Carbon cycle: nature's closed loop
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and trace one carbon atom round the loop: air to plant to animal to soil and back to air.

bullets: Deforestation removes a carbon sink while carbon dioxide piles up in the air
Replanting pushes back by restoring the sink
slides.heading: Humans tip the balance
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and name each change as it lands: sink lost, carbon dioxide rising, a warmer planet - then replanting pushing back.

bullets: Energy escapes as heat at every link and never loops back to the producer
Nutrients do loop: plant to animal to soil and back to plant
slides.heading: A common mistake: energy is recycled like nutrients
slides.notes: Play scene 5 and ask the class to state the difference in one sentence each: energy flows through, nutrients go round.

bullets: Suppose the grass holds 100 units of energy and the rabbit gains only about 10
If energy were recycled, the missing 90 would return to the grass - but it left as heat, so the claim fails
slides.heading: Worked example: testing the recycling claim on one link
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, only about a tenth passes up. Step 2, the rest is lost as heat and cannot feed the grass again, so energy is not recycled.

bullets: In pairs: list three things in an ecosystem that loop and one that only flows
Then swap and check: did anyone put energy in the looping list?
slides.heading: Your turn: separate flow from loop
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for energy wrongly listed as looping, then take two pairs' answers.

bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says energy is recycled
Name the one-way flow and the heat loss to earn full credit
slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers separate the one-way energy flow from the nutrient loop.
